best_plan.name: p2
best_plan.rationale: Plan p2 achieved the best cost-quality trade-off: it matched the highest observed quality (f1_score 0.6, same as p1) while being much cheaper ($0.0038764 vs $0.0241854) and faster (5.54s vs 19.12s). It also outperformed p3 on quality while still costing less.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model used observed mean cost and latency by operator type and model, which quickly showed that sem_map was by far the most expensive and slowest operator, while ordinary filter/project/limit were essentially free. That pushed plan design toward p2, which removed sem_map and relied on cheap exact filters plus a lightweight sem_filter and sem_join with Gemini Flash Lite. Trying a stronger model in p3 raised cost without improving quality, confirming that the cheaper semantic operators were the better choice here.

plan_codes.p1:
positive = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_positive", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
positive.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
positive.sem_filter(
    "This movie review is overall positive toward the movie.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)

negative = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_negative", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
negative.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
negative.sem_filter(
    "This movie review is overall negative toward the movie.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)

pipeline = positive.sem_join(
    negative,
    "These two rows are reviews of the same movie, and the first review is positive while the second review is negative.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE
)
pipeline.sem_map(
    [
        {"name": "idx_out", "type": str, "description": "The shared movie idx for the pair."},
        {"name": "reviewId_first", "type": str, "description": "The reviewId of the first review in the pair."},
        {"name": "reviewId_second", "type": str, "description": "The reviewId of the second review in the pair."}
    ],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE
)
pipeline.project(["idx_out", "reviewId_first", "reviewId_second"])
pipeline.limit(10)
pipeline
